title: Controller & View — One Fact, Four Checkpoints
description: Drills a single core fact about the CodeIgniter Controller-View relationship through four sections, each with micro-checks and a differently-formatted checkpoint.
coreFact: The Controller receives the request, runs the logic, and calls $this->load->view() to hand data to a View, which renders the HTML. Logic stays in the Controller; presentation stays in the View.
congratsText: Controller runs the logic, View renders the output — you've got it from every angle.
objectives: Identify the Controller as the entry point that answers an incoming request
Apply $this->load->view() to render a View from inside a Controller
Pass prepared data from a Controller into a View using an array
Distinguish Controller responsibilities from View responsibilities
recap: A Controller method is what the URL actually reaches, and it decides which View to load
$this->load->view('name') is the call that hands control from the Controller to the View
Data is prepared in the Controller and passed as an array, whose keys become variables in the View
Logic belongs in the Controller; the View only displays what it was given

chunks.text: When a browser requests a URL, CodeIgniter routes it to a Controller method — not to a View file directly.

check.question: What does a URL request reach first?

chunks.text: The Controller runs whatever logic the request needs, then decides which View should be shown.

check.question: Who decides which View gets shown?

chunks.text: A View never runs on its own — it only produces output because a Controller loaded it.

check.question: Can a View render without a Controller loading it?
options: Yes, it runs on its own

quiz.question: What is the Controller's role in relation to the View?
options: It receives the request and loads the View to produce output
It stores the finished HTML markup that gets sent to the browser
It replaces the View entirely once the app is deployed to production
It is generated automatically from whichever View file was requested

chunks.text: The call that hands off from Controller to View is $this->load->view('filename').
The filename passed in matches a file inside the application/views folder, written without the .php extension.

check.question: Do you include .php in the view name?

chunks.text: By default the loaded View's HTML is sent straight to the browser as part of the response.

check.question: Where does the View's HTML go by default?

quiz.question: Arrange the steps of a Controller-to-View request flow in order.
tokens: The View's HTML is sent back to the browser
The browser requests a URL mapped to a Controller method
The Controller method runs its logic
correctOrder: The browser requests a URL mapped to a Controller method
The Controller method runs its logic
The View's HTML is sent back to the browser

chunks.text: A Controller prepares values in an array and passes that array as the second argument to the view loader.

check.question: How is data handed to a View?

chunks.text: Each array key becomes a plain variable inside the View — a key named title becomes $title.

check.question: A key named 'user' becomes what in the View?

chunks.text: The View only ever sees what the Controller chose to pass in — it cannot reach back for more.

check.question: Can a View fetch extra data on its own?

quiz.question: Type the line that loads the View 'home' and passes $data into it.

chunks.text: A View's only job is to display values — echoing them, looping over them, formatting them for the page.
Calculations, database calls, and decisions belong in the Controller, before the View is ever loaded.

check.question: Where does a price calculation belong?

chunks.text: This split is what keeps a project maintainable — you can redesign the page without touching the logic.

check.question: Why keep logic and display separate?

quiz.question: What is wrong with this View file?
options: It computes a discounted total instead of just displaying one
It uses a foreach loop, which is not permitted inside any View file
It echoes a variable, which should always be handled by the Controller
It is missing a closing PHP tag at the very bottom of the file
